findings.description: `metadata` defaults to a shared dict `{}`, and `put` calls `metadata.setdefault("content-type", ...)` on it. The first put without metadata stores a guessed content type in the shared default, so every later put without metadata reuses that type, e.g. a .png then a .pdf gets image/png. A caller-supplied dict is also mutated.
findings.suggestion: Use `metadata: dict[str, str] | None = None` and build a copy: `meta = dict(metadata or {}); meta.setdefault(...)`.
findings.title: Mutable default argument is mutated by setdefault

findings.description: The metadata file is replaced before the blob is written. If the blob write fails, or a concurrent reader calls head in between, the old blob is paired with the new metadata. A new key whose blob write failed leaves an orphaned metadata file. The two atomic replaces are not atomic together.
findings.suggestion: Write the blob first, then the metadata, or clean up the metadata on failure.
findings.title: Metadata written before blob; failed blob write leaves inconsistent state

findings.description: `is_file()` followed by `read_text` is a check-then-act race with a concurrent delete, which raises FileNotFoundError. Corrupt JSON raises JSONDecodeError. Both escape instead of falling back to defaults.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the read and parse in try/except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError) and fall back to {}.
findings.title: head can fail on a missing or corrupt metadata file
